CC.scope: Direct 2026-07-28 extension requirements, with inherited core authorization and adopted-reference sections separately inventoried below. Host duties and unadopted profiles do not count as library passes.

EMA.scope: Direct 2026-07-28 extension requirements, with inherited core authorization and adopted-reference sections separately inventoried below. Host duties and unadopted profiles do not count as library passes.

IDJAG.scope: Draft-04 sections 3 through 9: bearer client exchange and helper behavior, IdP/resource-AS/host duties, and explicitly unadopted SAML subject mapping, rich authorization and DPoP. Appendices and IANA registration instructions are context, not library assertions.

TASKS.scope: Initial named regression requirements; official server checks are gated separately. Complete clause/schema mapping and client interop inventory remain pending.

CORE.scope: 2026-07-28 core requirement bundles and section dispositions, including the official schema, optional/deprecated retained features and host duties. Legacy revision inventories are outside this source scope. Complete inventory is not complete executable qualification; partial rows identify limits.

RFC6749.scope: Sections 2.2, 3.3, 4.4, 5.1 and 5.2 as used by client credentials, enterprise exchange and OAuth errors. Other grant types and AS operation are outside this dependency scope.

RFC6750.scope: Sections 2.1, 3 and 5 for HTTP bearer token transmission, challenges and token handling. Query/form token transmission is not adopted.

RFC7523.scope: Sections 2, 3 and 5 for JWT client authentication and authorization grants. Issuer trust, replay and issuing policy are separated from signature helpers.

RFC8414.scope: Sections 2, 3 and 6 for AS metadata publication/discovery/validation. Signed metadata is not adopted.

RFC8693.scope: Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 4 for enterprise token exchange. Arbitrary delegation chains are not adopted.

RFC8707.scope: Section 2 and security considerations for single-resource MCP token requests. Multiple-resource token issuance remains host policy.

RFC9207.scope: Sections 2.1 through 2.4 for metadata advertisement and authorization response issuer validation.

RFC9728.scope: Sections 2 through 5 and 7 for protected-resource metadata discovery, validation, challenges and resource binding. Signed metadata is not adopted.

OAUTH21.scope: Draft-13 sections 1.5, 2, 3, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5 and 7 in the adopted authorization-code, confidential client-credentials and bearer profiles; AS issuance and deployment duties remain host-owned.

OAUTH21_REFRESH.scope: Draft-14 section 4.3, explicitly referenced by core refresh-token confidentiality guidance. Other draft-14 changes are not adopted over draft-13.

CIMD00.scope: Draft-00 sections 3 through 6 for core client metadata documents and their host/AS requirements. This is the revision incorporated by core 2026-07-28.

CIMD01.scope: Draft-01 section 6.2 only, incorporated by Enterprise for optional private_key_jwt client metadata. Other draft-01 changes are not silently adopted.

RFC7591.scope: Sections 2 and 3 and security considerations for optional legacy DCR requests, responses and error handling. Registration management is not adopted.

OIDC_DISCOVERY.scope: Provider configuration discovery and validation sections 3 and 4 as an alternative to RFC8414; initial user SSO and full OIDC Relying Party behavior are host-owned.

OIDC_REGISTRATION.scope: Section 2 application_type and redirect registration constraints inherited by optional DCR. Other OIDC registration profiles are not adopted.

requirements.requirement: An adopted extension inherits the extension and core authorization requirements.
requirements.notes: Adopted core/reference sections have scoped dispositions. The matrix marks implemented client roles separately from broad inherited bundles, partial executable evidence and host/AS obligations; no full-system compliance claim.

requirements.requirement: Client credentials are pre-registered; DCR is not used.
requirements.notes: Authorization-code DCR remains separate.

requirements.requirement: Client credentials requests authenticate using a client secret or JWT.
requirements.notes: POST is supported as a configured secret method; AS metadata has separate obligations.

requirements.requirement: JWT authentication uses the client-assertion type and signed assertion profile.
requirements.notes: Named builder/verifier, independent jose peer, SDK helper and real Keycloak JWT cases qualify the adopted client-authentication profile. RFC7523.POLICY retains AS trust, provisioning and replay duties; these are not claimed as client implementation.

requirements.requirement: Select an interoperable advertised signing algorithm before sending an assertion.
requirements.notes: Client negotiation check; the explicit metadata MUST belongs to the AS.

requirements.requirement: Supporting AS metadata advertises private_key_jwt or client_secret_basic.
requirements.notes: Metadata helper is configurable; it does not implement a complete token-issuing AS.

requirements.requirement: An AS supporting JWT authentication publishes signing algorithms.
requirements.notes: Host must configure and enforce its advertised methods and algorithms.

requirements.requirement: Discover the resource AS and obtain a resource-bound token before authenticated MCP use.
requirements.notes: Named discovery binding contracts plus real Keycloak Basic/JWT token and mounted Arbor client/server cases. Provider qualification is confined to the configured client-credentials profiles on loopback HTTP; production DNS/TLS and AS deployment policy remain separate.

requirements.requirement: Protect credentials, tokens, storage and communications.
requirements.notes: CORE.AUTH_SECURITY, RFC6750.STORAGE, RFC7523.POLICY and OAUTH.DEPLOYMENT record adopted cross-cutting dispositions; host storage, TLS and deployment policy remain separate duties.

requirements.requirement: Obtain the initial identity assertion from the configured enterprise IdP.
requirements.notes: Host owns initial login, SAML validation, registration and administrator policy.

requirements.requirement: Exchange the identity assertion for an ID-JAG with audience equal to the resource-AS issuer.
requirements.notes: Both orchestrators exercise the selected subject exchange, target AS/resource binding and separate IdP credentials against the verifying independent peer; initial SSO and IdP issuance policy are host-owned.

requirements.requirement: Authenticate the exchange when the IdP registration requires authentication.
requirements.notes: Both orchestrators have named Basic/POST/JWT, method/algorithm/configuration/issuer binding and rejected-authentication contracts. Independent JWT exchanges are recorded under EMA.EXCHANGE; production IdP registration/policy is separate.

requirements.requirement: Support the selected subject-token profile, including the SAML-to-refresh-token transition.
requirements.notes: Initial SAML SSO, XML signature validation and IdP mapping policy remain host-owned.

requirements.requirement: A present resource identifies the MCP server.
requirements.notes: Resource absent is a separate explicitly configured profile.

requirements.requirement: The profile permits an ID-JAG resource claim to be absent.
requirements.notes: Default remains strict. Host still enforces resource-restricted token issuance.

requirements.requirement: Validate signature, audience, expiry, typed header and required ID-JAG claims.
requirements.notes: Named signature/audience/resource/expiry/type, creation/scope/lifetime and each-required-key rejection contracts qualify the helper claim-validation role. Semantic identity/tenant resolution, authenticated-client authorization and replay consumption remain host/IdP/AS duties under the separate IDJAG policy bundles.

requirements.requirement: Present the ID-JAG as a JWT bearer grant and authenticate with the resource-AS registration.
requirements.notes: Optional as_auth Basic/POST/JWT has explicit issuer/client/endpoint bindings; legacy behavior retained when absent.

requirements.requirement: A non-preregistered client can use a configured metadata document identifier.
requirements.notes: Both orchestrators preserve discovered CIMD support and authenticate with the metadata-document client ID. Independent AS fetches metadata/inline or URL JWKS and rejects identity/key mismatches. Explicit fixture transport mapping does not qualify production DNS/TLS or a vendor CIMD AS.

requirements.requirement: Apply enterprise trust policy and issue a token restricted to the authorized MCP resource.
requirements.notes: The grant helper does not provide token issuance, SAML policy or a complete OAuth AS.

requirements.requirement: Recognize the ID-JAG authorization_grant_profiles_supported indicator.
requirements.notes: Discovered profile and grant contradictions fail before either token leg. Explicit host-selected endpoints have no metadata to contradict; older metadata may omit the optional profile indicator.

requirements.requirement: Bind issuer, subject, client and tenant to the appropriate trusted registration.
requirements.notes: Host registration/policy responsibility; helpers alone do not qualify a multi-tenant AS.

requirements.requirement: Process token responses and OAuth errors without substituting another issuer or credential.
requirements.notes: Named cases reject wrong/missing exchanged token types and missing AS access_token, preserve AS OAuth denial, and reject failed IdP authentication without cross-authority credential retries. Broader mixed client/issuer and AS response/issuance duties remain separately scoped under RFC6749.RESPONSES, RFC8693.RESPONSE and CORE.AUTH_ISSUER.

requirements.requirement: Accept nullable ttlMs while preserving its required wire field.
requirements.notes: Initial scoped requirement evidence; not a complete Tasks specification qualification.

requirements.requirement: Mirror taskId in the required request routing header.
requirements.notes: Initial scoped requirement evidence; not a complete Tasks specification qualification.

requirements.requirement: Return invalid-params for unknown task identifiers without disclosing ownership.
requirements.notes: Initial scoped requirement evidence; not a complete Tasks specification qualification.

requirements.requirement: Keep input request keys unique throughout the task lifetime.
requirements.notes: Initial scoped requirement evidence; not a complete Tasks specification qualification.

requirements.requirement: Represent execution errors as a failed task, including while input is outstanding.

requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Modern success envelopes identify complete/input_required or a negotiated extension result type; reject unrecognized types, preserving the specified legacy absent-type behavior.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Preserve declared schema dialects and validate declared/default2020-12 schemas and instances. Reject unsupported dialects; do not silently accept unsupported vocabularies.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Never dereference network $ref by default; explicit opt-in is bounded by host/network policy, time and size. Unresolved references must not silently make validation permissive; bound expensive schema composition.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Carry required version/capabilities on every request, reject missing values and undeclared required capabilities with specified errors; serverInfo/clientInfo are self-reported. Preserve caller metadata and subscription correlation.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Use reserved-prefix and key-name rules for metadata/extensions. Trace context values must follow W3C formats when supplied; self-reported identities must not drive authorization.
requirements.notes: Application/extension authors own custom metadata and trace values; generic map preservation is not validation or authorization.

requirements.requirement: Icon-rendering consumers support required image formats and securely validate schemes/origins/redirects, MIME/content, bounds and credential-free retrieval; treat metadata and bytes as untrusted.
requirements.notes: Arbor transports icon descriptors; it does not fetch or render icons. UI/network image qualification belongs to the host.

requirements.requirement: Implement server/discover; reject unsupported versions with the supported list, select/retry a mutually supported version or surface an error. Extension negotiation must fall back to core or reject unsupported requests.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Keep legacy initialize semantics distinct from per-request modern semantics; dual-era stdio probes and HTTP error inspection determine eligible fallback and cached era observations without replaying an operation in another era.
requirements.notes: Existing four-mode/strict-era tests remain authoritative; the official modern harness does not exhaust downgrade and cache-failure paths.

requirements.requirement: Use newline-delimited JSON-RPC UTF-8 frames with no embedded literal newlines; stdout/stdin carry only protocol messages, stderr is separate, and modern server interactions use MRTR rather than standalone requests.
requirements.notes: Existing framing and cross-language stdio suites remain in CI. The official HTTP harness is not stdio evidence; the named case checks frame-start BOM handling only.

requirements.requirement: Cancel stdio requests by ID; close streams gracefully, bound termination and restart unexpected exits; re-establish subscriptions after restart and distinguish modern probing from legacy initialization.
requirements.notes: Process cleanup and restart are covered by existing transport lifecycle/interop suites, not duplicated here or certified by the HTTP conformance artifact.

requirements.requirement: Provide a POST endpoint; send one request/notification per POST with both JSON/SSE Accept types, support JSON and SSE replies, accept notifications with empty202, and never send independent modern server requests.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Validate Origin and reject invalid origins with403; configure authentication and safe local listener binding. Custom transports preserve base wire/lifecycle guarantees and channel security.
requirements.notes: The official scenario tests Origin/DNS-rebinding rejection. Listener binding, TLS and deployment authentication are host responsibilities.

requirements.requirement: Send per-request version/method/name headers, including encoded non-ASCII/sentinel values; compare decoded header values to the body case-sensitively with case-insensitive names, returning400/-32020 on mismatch and404/-32601 for unknown methods.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Validate x-mcp-header names, uniqueness, primitive/safe-integer types and properties-only reachability; omit null/absent values, encode unsafe/sentinel values, reject malformed definitions individually, validate server header/body equality and refresh schemas after mismatch.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: An HTTP response-stream disconnect cancels its originating request; stop work/messages and terminate final responses. Proxy buffering should be disabled for SSE; legacy GET/session/DELETE rules do not apply to modern connections.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Use input_required only on eligible methods, include inputRequests or requestState, uniquely identify supported inputs and require declared capabilities. Missing input can be requested again; ignore unnecessary extra input and validate recognized responses.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Fulfill input requests before retrying; echo opaque requestState unchanged only when supplied, use a fresh JSON-RPC ID and isolate inputs/state to the original logical operation.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Treat retry state as attacker-controlled, verify integrity and reject tampering; bind principal, expiry and originating request where needed, and enforce server-side single-use when semantics require it.
requirements.notes: Tamper assertions are official. Actual principal binding, replay configuration and business single-use policy retain existing local coverage and host duties.

requirements.requirement: Use unique active string/integer progress tokens, increasing numeric progress, optional total/message, and no progress after completion or for unrelated requests. Frequency/rate limits are policy; progress can reset a request timeout within an absolute cap.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Cancel only issued in-flight requests, ignore stale/unknown races and late replies, release work/resources, and bound per-call/absolute deadlines. Server cancellation notifications are restricted to subscriptions.
requirements.notes: Existing cancellation, progress and lifecycle tests remain in CI; official core scenarios do not exhaust these request-ownership/race invariants.

requirements.requirement: Send acknowledgment first per subscription ID, preserve correlation on all notifications, honor only requested filters, isolate concurrent subscriptions, handle graceful completion and reconnect/re-establishment after disconnect.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Declare tools, list the request-authorized catalog deterministically, call by unique names with valid JSON Schema objects, distinguish tool errors from protocol errors and preserve content/annotations/output schema semantics. Treat annotations as untrusted and disambiguate aggregated names independently of serverInfo.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Validate and authorize tool input, bound calls and rates, sanitize outputs, and provide user approval, audit and output-schema validation according to host policy; do not mirror secrets into headers.
requirements.notes: Arbor supplies validators, timeouts and middleware. Application access policy, semantic output sanitization, names and human approval cannot be established by fixture tool results.

requirements.requirement: Declare resources, list authorized descriptors/templates, return valid text or base64 blob contents with URI/MIME/annotations, support filtered change/update streams, validate resource identifiers and reject missing resources with-32602 rather than empty contents.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Choose appropriate standard/custom URI schemes, validate/sanitize resource URIs and file paths, check permissions and sensitive-resource access, and define actual resource availability.
requirements.notes: Application resource handlers own filesystem/resource semantics and traversal protection; a generic URI transport is not a sandbox.

requirements.requirement: Declare prompts; list authorized descriptors, resolve arguments and content messages (text/image/audio/resource links/embedded resources), respect pagination/capabilities and signal filtered list changes.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Declare completions, support prompt/resource-template references, return bounded values/total/hasMore, and validate inputs/errors. Relevance, fuzziness, debouncing, rate and access policy belong to the host.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Pass opaque cursors unchanged, accept empty-string cursors, make no fixed-size assumptions, stop only at missing/null nextCursor and handle invalid cursors without silent partial success.
requirements.notes: The existing pagination helper test covers opaque cursors across all four list helpers; official list scenarios do not certify adversarial pagination.

requirements.requirement: Supply nonnegative ttlMs and public/private cacheScope on eligible complete results; partition by method/parameters and authorization for private data, never cache MRTR inputs/state, re-fetch stale data and invalidate from notifications. Pagination pages have separate keys; polling requires backoff/jitter.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Retained deprecated logging uses declared capability and per-request logLevel; emit only at/above that level on the originating response stream, never a subscription. Validate levels, bound volume and exclude credentials/PII.
requirements.notes: Existing request-scoped logging and redaction tests remain in CI. The official modern core scenario list has no dedicated logging scenario; application log content still requires host review.

requirements.requirement: Declare supported form/url modes, default omitted mode to form, validate limited schemas/actions/responses, support MRTR re-prompts and handle decline/cancel. URL acceptance is consent, not proof of completed out-of-band interaction.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Keep secrets out of forms/URLs and MCP payloads; do not prefetch/open URLs without explicit user consent, display full requesting server/URL, isolate browser contents, bind state and out-of-band identity to the initiating verified user, and keep third-party tokens separate.
requirements.notes: The library dispatches callbacks; the host owns UI, browser behavior, initial authorization and external credential storage. Form-mode semantic sensitivity cannot be inferred from a schema alone.

requirements.requirement: Retained deprecated sampling declares capabilities (including tool/context support), validates role/content/tool-use-result pairing, respects maxTokens and model/tool-choice constraints; user approval, safe data, iteration limits and provider behavior are host-owned.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Retained deprecated roots declares per-request capability and file:// identifiers; handle roots via MRTR. Hosts validate paths/permissions, monitor availability, obtain consent and enforce root boundaries; roots metadata alone grants no filesystem sandbox.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Separate host/client/server responsibilities; user consent, LLM approval, trust, isolation, privacy and application-specific access controls accompany capability and wire validation.
requirements.notes: Architectural guidance and trust/safety principles are mapped explicitly, not treated as wire assertion passes.

requirements.requirement: Use the pinned official schema definitions for message/result/input/content fields and all adopted optional forms, including required fields and discriminated unions. Data-shape validity is distinct from semantic authorization.
requirements.notes: Schema copies/drift and existing message/input validators are reused. A schema dialect scenario is not exhaustive validation of every definition or negative instance.

requirements.requirement: Publish PRM with an AS; prefer challenged metadata URLs, otherwise ordered resource well-known URLs. Support RFC8414 and OIDC discovery with path-aware ordering and exact resource/issuer validation.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Select pre-registration, CIMD or optional deprecated DCR with declared priority; validate HTTPS metadata identity/required fields, appropriate application_type/redirects and exact issuer-bound credentials. Re-register or reject on AS changes.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Prioritize authoritative challenged scopes, otherwise metadata guidance; accumulate grants and bounded step-up retries without assuming challenged/advertised set relationships. Hosts define hierarchy and all scopes for an operation.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Record validated issuer with PKCE/state; compare a present form-decoded iss exactly without URL normalization and require it when advertised. Reject missing/mismatched issuer before token exchange or acting on error responses.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios exercise expected, absent, unadvertised, wrong and normalized-variant issuer responses.

requirements.requirement: Include the authoritative canonical MCP resource identifier in authorization/token requests regardless of AS feature advertisement, and keep issued credentials/resource partitions bound to the selected AS.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Send tokens only in Authorization on every HTTP request, never URI queries or upstream passthrough; validate audience/issuer/expiry/permissions before work, return401 for invalid tokens and403 for insufficient scope.
requirements.notes: Existing authorization/provider/transport tests remain authoritative. The client Auth conformance scenarios do not certify arbitrary resource-server policy or upstream token separation.

requirements.requirement: Protect refresh tokens, advertise refresh grant as appropriate, request offline_access only if supported and do not assume issuance; resources should not require offline_access. Rotation, persistence and reauthentication policy belong to host/AS.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Use HTTPS endpoints and approved redirects, PKCE/S256 with discovered support and state validation, exact redirect registration, issuer binding, secure storage and restricted token audience; hosts enforce consent for proxies, CIMD trust and safe deployment policy.
requirements.notes: Existing PKCE, callback, endpoint and credential-store tests are reused below. A general OAuth client does not supply deployment trust policy or proxy consent UI.

requirements.requirement: Use the registered client identity and one negotiated authentication method, exact registered redirect, code/verifier/state and form-encoded token requests. Bind code flow and credentials to the discovered issuer.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Generate fresh PKCE verifier/challenge, use S256, verify advertised support and validate callback state/issuer before transmitting a code.
requirements.notes: Existing PKCE-pair compliance assertions are reused. Five new metadata/fallback regressions reject unsupported automatic flows; host/provider code and AS authorization issuance remain separate.

requirements.requirement: Client credentials is confidential-client-only with authenticated client identity, form grant_type and scope; no end-user redirect or dynamic registration on the adopted extension path.
requirements.notes: CC extension requires preregistration; AS credential provisioning and grant issuance are host-owned.

requirements.requirement: Authenticate refresh requests where applicable, bind the refresh grant to the same client/AS and restrict scope; protect/revoke/rotate refresh credentials as required for the deployment.
requirements.notes: Client refresh handling is implemented; token-family replay detection, rotation and durable storage policy belong to AS/host.

requirements.requirement: Transmit bearer credentials over protected channels only to their intended resource; validate inbound tokens and token scope, protect storage and handle authentication/authorization errors without credential disclosure.
requirements.notes: See core Auth token and RFC6750 rows; complete AS/host operations are not asserted by the generic helpers.

requirements.requirement: Enforce TLS, secure endpoints/redirects, client identity/consent, code and refresh replay protections, least privilege, credential storage and lifecycle, open-redirect/mix-up protection and abuse controls.
requirements.notes: Protocol helpers do not deploy an OAuth authorization server or user-agent. Existing endpoint/state/issuer controls are separately mapped; remaining deployment duties are explicit.

requirements.requirement: Keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage as referenced by core; issuer/client binding and rotation cannot be weakened by refresh acquisition.
requirements.notes: Only the core-referenced draft14 refresh section is adopted; no wholesale upgrade from draft13 is implied.

requirements.requirement: Client IDs are AS-scoped; scope is case-sensitive space-delimited text, and client-credentials requests authenticate the confidential client.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Process successful token fields and OAuth token errors according to their types/semantics; AS responses carry appropriate error/status/cache headers and never leak grant secrets.
requirements.notes: The named exchange regressions test typed enterprise responses. General OAuth error/status/cache-control issuance is an AS duty and not certified by them.

requirements.requirement: Use the Bearer Authorization header, parse WWW-Authenticate challenges, and distinguish invalid_request/invalid_token/insufficient_scope with401/403 and needed scopes.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Protect bearer token confidentiality in storage and transport, restrict audience/scope and prevent replay or leakage through logging, URLs and forwarding.
requirements.notes: Arbor credential structs redact inspection and transport requests are issuer-bound; deployments must choose persistent storage, TLS and resource authorization policy.

requirements.requirement: Send the JWT-bearer client_assertion_type plus assertion; bind iss/sub to client identity and aud to the expected AS/token endpoint, with signature/expiry and configured algorithm validation.
requirements.notes: Named existing assertion cases and independent verifying peers exercise the adopted client assertion profile.

requirements.requirement: Send JWT bearer grant_type/assertion and optional scope; validate signature, trusted issuer/subject, audience, expiry and grant/client authorization before resource token issuance.
requirements.notes: ID-JAG helper returns claims, not an authorization decision. The host validates authenticated client binding, subject resolution, replay, permissions and issuance policy.

requirements.requirement: Pin trusted algorithms/keys and authenticating client identity, validate claim types, reject unknown issuers/audiences and expired assertions, and implement a suitable replay policy for assertion IDs.
requirements.notes: Signature/time/audience helpers are separately tested. Assertion replay storage and AS authorization policy are explicitly not supplied by the general JWT helpers.

requirements.requirement: Publish appropriate issuer/endpoints/auth/grant metadata; fetch path-aware well-known configuration and reject a metadata issuer not identical to the intended issuer.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Use authenticated HTTPS discovery, validate issuer before endpoints, and apply trust and network controls to fetched metadata and credentials.
requirements.notes: The relabelled existing test checks exact endpoint origin/issuer policy; deployment trust and TLS remain host-owned.

requirements.requirement: Discover PRM by challenge or resource well-known URL, validate its resource identity and usable authorization_servers, and use discovered metadata for AS and scope selection.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Bind protected metadata to the intended resource, validate issuer/endpoints and restrict token audience; unauthenticated metadata must not select a destination for unrelated secrets.
requirements.notes: Relabelled existing credential-policy test rejects mismatched pre-registered issuer before secret resolution; TLS and resource policy still belong to the host.

requirements.requirement: Use an absolute fragment-free intended resource identifier in authorization/token requests and require resource-restricted tokens, rejecting invalid targets and preserving exact resource identity.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: AS advertises issuer response support and emits iss as appropriate; clients compare a present form-decoded issuer exactly and require it when advertised before processing code or errors.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Use token-exchange grant_type with exact requested/subject token types, selected subject token and resource-AS audience/resource/scope. Keep subject token and client-authentication credentials distinct.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Qualify issued_token_type, token_type and access_token before consuming an exchange; the ID-JAG profile uses N_A and its exact issued type, and SAML transition must yield a refresh token.
requirements.notes: Existing regressions reject wrong/missing response types and prevent the next token leg.

requirements.requirement: Validate subject/actor tokens and requested audiences/scopes using local trust/policy. Actor/delegation chains and arbitrary token types are not enabled by passing opaque enterprise subjects.
requirements.notes: The adopted client supports only the documented OIDC/refresh/SAML-transition paths. Generic actor-token issuance/delegation is not a library qualification claim.

requirements.requirement: For optional deprecated DCR, send validated client metadata and handle required registered fields, generated client credentials and errors without silently relaxing redirect constraints.
requirements.notes: Client registration and application_type tests are reused. AS registration issuance/policy is host-owned.

requirements.requirement: Validate successful/error registration responses and protect returned secrets; authenticate and constrain registration according to AS policy rather than assuming arbitrary self-registration is trusted.
requirements.notes: Persisted registrations are partitioned by exact issuer. DCR access policy, initial-access tokens and registry operations are AS responsibilities.

requirements.requirement: Support OIDC well-known metadata as an alternative discovery path and validate the returned issuer exactly; MCP additionally requires discovered PKCE support before authorization-code flow.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Explicitly choose native/web application_type and valid redirect URIs, handle rejected registrations without a weakening retry, and preserve exact issuer registration binding.
requirements.notes: The core-adopted registration fields are covered; initial OIDC SSO, ID-token verification for host login and other OP/RP behavior remain outside this helper.

requirements.requirement: Use HTTPS client_id URLs with paths, exact metadata identity and required client_name/redirect_uris; validate JSON and registered redirect values, honor advertised support and caching/trust policy.
requirements.notes: Arbor provides metadata helpers and client selection. Production hosting, AS metadata caching and redirect consent are host duties.

requirements.requirement: Constrain metadata fetches against SSRF/resource exhaustion, validate client/redirect origins and domain trust, show localhost/redirect risks and never treat URL ownership as unconditional client trust.
requirements.notes: This library is not a complete CIMD authorization server or consent UI; no vendor/client certification follows from its metadata helper.

requirements.requirement: Optional enterprise private_key_jwt authentication uses client metadata/JWKS and separately authenticated AS client identity; grant assertion and client assertion are distinct.
requirements.notes: Separate IdP/AS credentials and CIMD client-ID assertions are qualified by contracts and an independent AS fetching document and inline/URL keys, with identity/key rejection cases. Explicit fixture transport mapping is separate from production DNS/TLS and vendor CIMD qualification.

requirements.requirement: Use typed signed ID-JAGs with issuer, subject, audience, client_id, unique jti, exp and iat; preserve optional resource/scope and relevant identity claims while rejecting invalid signature/audience/time.
requirements.notes: Helpers cover signature/required-key/time/audience/resource checks, not semantic validation of every optional claim, subject identity, authenticated-client authorization or replay.

requirements.requirement: Resolve the same end user across sub/sub_id/aud_sub and issuer/tenant namespaces; construct/compare the full SAML NameID identifier according to trusted mappings and bind the target AS client_id.
requirements.notes: Arbor does not implement a SAML identity federation, tenant directory or subject resolver. Opaque SAML-to-refresh input is not NameID/XML validation.

requirements.requirement: Obtain a trusted initial identity assertion, use selected ID-token/refresh subject with target AS audience/resource/scope and distinct IdP client credentials, and qualify the typed exchange response before AS redemption.
requirements.notes: Official scenarios cover the named wire assertions; the broader bundle is not a certification of every clause or host policy.

requirements.requirement: Authenticate the requesting client, validate original subject token, enforce issuer/client/audience and tenant/admin policy, and issue a short-lived grant only for permitted target resources/scopes.
requirements.notes: The independent peer verifies its own fixture policy. It is not a production IdP or certification of all IdP policies.

requirements.requirement: Redeem at the audience AS using JWT-bearer grant and separate client authentication. AS validates trusted issuer, subject resolution, replay, authenticated client_id, resource/scope/details and issuance policy before granting access.
requirements.notes: The grant handler returns validated claims only. It does not authenticate the token-endpoint caller, consume jti, resolve tenants/subjects or authorize/issue a resource token.

requirements.requirement: Resource-AS responses report granted resource/scope/details; normally renew through a fresh IdP grant rather than AS refresh token. Hosts obtain a new identity assertion or reauthenticate if the original is expired.
requirements.notes: Initial SSO, user reauthentication and AS refresh/issuance policy are deliberately host-owned; no background renewal guarantee is implied by one exchange helper call.

requirements.requirement: SAML-to-refresh exchange uses the supported SAML token type then a refresh-subject ID-JAG request. IdP validates XML/signature/audience-to-client mapping; initial SSO may request openid/offline_access.
requirements.notes: The independent fixture uses an opaque SAML token. Host/IdP SAML validation and actual SSO are not supplied or qualified.

requirements.requirement: Advertise grant-profile/token types consistently with the corresponding grant_types. Do not use profile advertisement to disclose issuer-specific trust relationships.
requirements.notes: IdP metadata publication is host-owned; Arbor publishes/checks the adopted resource-AS profile. A profile alone cannot override contradictory grants.

requirements.requirement: Prefer confidential clients, respect step-up and cross-domain trust, issue a new grant per downstream AS, keep issuer acceptance confidential, trust validated iss rather than sub_id.issuer, and minimize disclosed identifiers.
requirements.notes: Local trusted_idps and separate issuer-bound credentials are building blocks. They are not a trust federation, consent policy, step-up flow or subject resolver.

requirements.requirement: When adopting actor delegation, rich authorization, multiple resources or sender-constrained grants, enforce their profile processing and proof-of-possession requirements; never treat a cnf claim as proof.
requirements.notes: Arbor does not implement DPoP, actor delegation or RAR policy. A host accepting these claims must validate them before access-token issuance; signature helper success does not authorize them.
